The singular feature that got stranded is now clear in the tree: the measured routed-MoE implementation still exists only under `bench/` and the obsolete standalone `xonotic/planner/plan.py`; the live Gram policy never calls it. Likewise, the hardware benchmark’s `XᵀX` is a residual-basis Gram of width R, while the live policy only forms a 256×256 player Gram at rank 128. Those are different workloads, so the current hardware claim is not merely unmeasured—it is architecturally disconnected.

I’m restoring that missing path into the learned policy itself: routed experts over live participant–instrument residual rows, followed by a nonlinear R×R residual Gram that feeds back into the IR and logits. The ordinary test shape stays small; the responder’s release defaults will be R=2048, 32 experts, FF=4096, top-2 routing.

The code confirms the disconnect precisely: the live Gram is only player×player at rank 128, while the 2048-wide MoE exists only in benchmark files. I’m making the large operator a residual over every player×instrument relation, before every live head, so it cannot become decorative telemetry or an algebraically removable side path.

The live-policy patch is in place now: top-2 routing, sorted gather-matmul experts, a nonlinear 2048×2048 residual-feature Gram, and a learned probe all sit before the action, value, and dynamics heads. The responder will report rank, actual expert occupancy, parameter bytes, Gram range/finite status, and whether the release-scale occupancy claim is met—not merely infer those from a benchmark.
